newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes firmer on technicals, weather.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes firmer on technicals, weather.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed firmer on Wednesday because of technical factors, bullish weekly data from the U.S., and signs of cold weather in the U.S. towards the weekend, traders said.
February gas oil ended the day $4 a tonne firmer at $204.50 a tonne and March Brent was 44 cents a barrel higher at 1805 GMT, trading at $22.69.
"There is nothing really new over here, we are just following the U.S." one IPE dealer said.
Latest data from the Energy Information Administration (EIA) showed a fall in U.S. middle distillate inventories of 2.5 million barrels over the week to January 24.
This was higher than had been expected earlier in the week but roughly in line with the latest weekly data released by the American Petroleum Institute (API).
Independent forecasters Weather Services Corp. (WSC) said on Wednesday: "The northeast will be cold through the week's end with higher heating demand."
WSC added that Europe would see colder temperatures towards the weekend.
Technical factors have added to the rally.
Charles Gray of Prudential-Bache futures said in a daily report: "Technically, support is building up below us as downward momentum dissipates."
Traders said that when the March Brent contract failed to break below $22.00 a barrel, traders had the confidence to cover some short positions in what had been seen as a relatively oversold market.
Dealers pegged next resistance for March Brent at $22.80, the day's high, and then at $23.00. -- Nicholas Shaxson, London newsroom +44 171 542 8167
